subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: What authorization state may a synchronous reader observe while the same process owns an in-flight exec-approval write transaction?
rationale: The choice between strict serialization, transaction-local prepared state, or stale committed policy determines whether a concurrent revocation can still authorize an exec and requires explicit authorization-owner intent.

options.title: Preserve transaction serialization
options.body: Add process-local ownership so only the writer's reentrant reads receive transaction-consistent state while unrelated readers remain fail-closed until commit.

options.title: Permit stale committed policy
options.body: Allow unrelated readers to use the prior persisted policy during a write and explicitly accept the resulting revocation window.

options.title: Redesign synchronous callers
options.body: Convert the affected decision paths to the async lock contract, accepting the broader caller and API refactor needed to remove mixed locking.

recommendation.title: Preserve transaction serialization
recommendation.body: Add process-local ownership so only the writer's reentrant reads receive transaction-consistent state while unrelated readers remain fail-closed until commit.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal covers the central exec-approval architecture and authorization behavior involved in this choice.
